question: Should tools.exec.denylist override ordinary full/off and durable trust while authorized elevated-full remains the explicit break-glass bypass?
rationale: This defines the permanent meaning of a new security/config surface and the highest-privilege exception; automation cannot choose that policy contract safely.

options.title: Accept the proposed contract
options.body: Keep deny-over-allow for ordinary execution, retain elevated-full as the documented break-glass path, and require exact-head integrated proof before merge.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Remove the elevated-full exception and update tests and docs so configured denylist matches always require a human decision.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the existing allowlist/full model and close or pause both implementation PRs until a different policy design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed contract
recommendation.body: Keep deny-over-allow for ordinary execution, retain elevated-full as the documented break-glass path, and require exact-head integrated proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans exec security semantics, public configuration, and existing elevated behavior owned by the central exec-policy area.
